note: P0.2 acceptance: the legacy in-source-layer placement reproduces a pre-array catalogue point BIT-IDENTICALLY. The array port rewrote how a plan reaches the solver for every driver, so the question is not whether the new path is better but whether the old one still exists -- 80,330 solves of back catalogue are only interpretable if it does.

reproduction.note: --stack skylake pins the historical lidded template (the default is now auto) and --no-array selects the in-source-layer placement. Everything else is the original command.

also_identical: the leakage-feedback residual trajectory printed to stderr matches digit for digit: iter 49 21.9424 -> 24.6929 K, iter 52 23.7690 -> 26.7467 K, iter 105 18.5093 -> 20.8400 K, iter 124 18.0042 -> 20.2718 K. The runaway is reached along the same path, not merely to the same verdict.
what_changed: the reproduced rows additionally carry placement="in_source_layer" where the originals carry no stamp at all. That is the intended difference and the whole point of the stamp: a row from before the port is identifiable by the ABSENCE of a placement, rather than by its date.
